The after_script in .gitlab/ci_templates/local-publish.yml uses plain "mkdir rpm-qa" to create the directory for the production-vs-pipeline RPM comparison.

Jobs extending .publish produce rpm-qa/ as an artifact. When a downstream job in the same pipeline (e.g. build-multi or a later arch build) downloads artifacts from earlier build-arches jobs, the rpm-qa/ directory already exists. This causes "mkdir rpm-qa" to fail with "File exists", and stale files from another arch comparison can produce a misleading RPM diff.

Fix: replace "mkdir" with "rm -rf && mkdir" to ensure a clean state.

The after_script in .gitlab/ci_templates/local-publish.yml uses plain "mkdir rpm-qa" to create the directory for the production-vs-pipeline RPM comparison. On runners that reuse workspaces (GIT_STRATEGY: fetch), this causes two problems:

1. "mkdir rpm-qa" fails with "File exists" because the directory was left behind by a previous pipeline run.

2. If one of the "buildah from" commands fails in the current run but succeeded in a previous run, the stale production.txt or pipeline.txt from the old run remains on disk. The diff then compares stale data against fresh data, producing a misleading RPM comparison.

Fix: replace "mkdir rpm-qa" with "rm -rf rpm-qa && mkdir rpm-qa" to ensure a clean state.

h2. Problem

Renovate opens MRs to bump Applecrumble components (Grafana image, plugins, base images), but they sit unmerged because there is no staging environment to validate against. Reviewers are reluctant to approve version bumps that go straight to production with no way to verify they don't break dashboards or datasources.

h2. Approach

Grafana is the first Applecrumble service to get a staging instance, since it is the most visible consumer and has the most Renovate MRs piling up. Other services (Loki, Prometheus, Alertmanager, etc.) will likely need staging deployments too, but Grafana on its own already unblocks meaningful testing — it can connect to the production backends via their external routes.

h2. Solution

Deploy a staging Grafana instance on the preprod cluster that mirrors production's dashboards, datasources, and folders. A CI job ({{grafana_data/deploy.sh}}) syncs the Git-backed configuration onto the staging instance, injecting datasource passwords from Vault.

The {{cki_tools.grafana}} upload tool is also switched from numeric-ID-based to UID-based datasource API endpoints, making YAML files portable across Grafana instances (production IDs differ from staging IDs).

h2. Deliverables

* Staging Grafana deployment on {{mpp-preprod/cki--applecrumble}}
* {{grafana_data/deploy.sh}} CI job to sync dashboards, datasources, folders, and org preferences
* UID-based datasource sync in {{cki_tools.grafana}} (fixes 500 errors from ID conflicts)
* Production cleanup: removed unused Loki Backend datasource, switched dashboard to Loki frontend, dropped unnecessary CA certs
* Grafana documentation page covering architecture, staging, backups, and datasource management

h2. Follow-up

Staging deployments for other Applecrumble services (Loki, Prometheus, Alertmanager, etc.) are not part of this task but will be needed to fully validate the stack end-to-end.

h2. Problem

The Applecrumble monitoring stack (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, memcached) deploys only to production ({{mpp-prod/cki--applecrumble}}) with no staging environment. Major Renovate version bumps have been sitting unmerged for over a month because there is no safe way to validate them:

* !4085: Grafana v12 -> v13 (one-way DB migration)
* !4089 + !4087: Prometheus v2 -> v3
* !4088: Loki v2 -> v3 (requires config rewrite)
* !4082, !4209: memcached bumps

h2. Approach

Grafana is the first Applecrumble service to get staging because it is the simplest -- it is a pure reader that queries Prometheus/Loki, so a staging Grafana pointing at production backends already validates dashboard rendering, plugin compatibility, and the v13 upgrade. Other services (Loki, Prometheus) will need their own staging deployments as follow-up work.

h2. Deliverables (this task)

* Staging Grafana deployment on {{mpp-preprod/cki--applecrumble}}
* {{grafana_data/deploy.sh}} CI job to sync dashboards, datasources, folders, and org preferences from git to staging
* UID-based datasource sync in {{cki_tools.grafana}} (numeric IDs differ between instances, causing 500 errors)
* Production cleanup: removed unused Loki Backend datasource, fixed dashboard datasource reference, dropped unnecessary CA certs
* Grafana documentation page

h2. Follow-up (not this task)

* Staging deployments for Prometheus, Loki, Alertmanager, memcached
* Cross-service reference templating (13 refs across 3 config files)
* S3 buckets + IAM for staging Loki storage
* Loki v3 config rewrite (removed keys, TSDB migration, {{cortex_*}} -> {{loki_*}} metric renames)

h2. MRs

* deployment-all: [!4221|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/cki-project/deployment-all/-/merge_requests/4221]
* cki-tools: [!2125|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/cki-tools/-/merge_requests/2125]

h2. Motivation

lxml is a C-extension wrapper around libxml2/libxslt. As a compiled dependency it has been a recurring source of pain, especially on RHEL 6 where prebuilt wheels are unavailable and building from source against the old system libraries fails. The history tells the story:

* *2024*: lxml pinned to 4.9.x because lxml 5 installation is broken on RHEL 6 ([infrastructure#305|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/infrastructure/-/issues/305]). A Python-version split was needed.
* *2025*: Constraints reworked after the RHEL 6 Python version was bumped to 3.11+ ([rhel-backports#3|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/rhel-backports/-/issues/3]).
* *2026-05*: CI needed a special container image ({{quay.io/cki/python}}) with lxml compilation dependencies just to run constraint verification ([pipeline-definition !2570|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2570]).
* *2026-06*: Renovate bumps lxml to v6, [pipeline-definition !2610|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2610] fails again.

Only two projects actually use lxml, and neither needs its full power.

----

h2. Safety Analysis

Three risks were identified and each has a mitigation:

h3. Risk 1: Whitespace in .text comparisons (beaker-jobwatch)

Dropping lxml's {{remove_blank_text=True}} means whitespace-only text nodes survive parsing. Most code uses substring checks ({{in}}) or {{json.loads}}, which tolerate whitespace. But one exact-match comparison is hazardous:

{code}if task.text == "External Watchdog Expired":{code}

*Mitigation:* Normalize to {{(task.text or "").strip() == "External Watchdog Expired"}}. This is safe to land pre-migration and protects against Beaker output format changes regardless.

h3. Risk 2: Three untested lxml-specific code paths (beaker-jobwatch)

All three paths using lxml-only APIs ({{xpath}}, {{getparent}}, {{getnext}}) have *zero test coverage*.

*Mitigation:* Add tests for these paths _before_ refactoring. Tests pass with lxml first, then pass again with stdlib -- proving equivalence.

h3. Risk 3: Losing schema validation safety net (kpet)

The lint block catches malformed XML and schema violations _before_ Beaker submission. Removing it shifts failure detection downstream.

*Mitigation:* Add {{xmllint}} validation to both kpet-db CI _and_ pipeline-definition's setup stage. This must land _before_ removing the lint block from kpet.

----

h2. Plan

h3. Step 1: beaker-jobwatch -- migrate to stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree (~5h)

*1a. Harden .text comparisons* (safe with lxml too, land first)
* {{task.text == "External Watchdog Expired"}} -> {{(task.text or "").strip() == "External Watchdog Expired"}}
* Guard {{result.text}} against {{None}} in {{get_destructive_tasks}}

*1b. Add tests for untested paths* (land before migration)
* HW mismatch: mock aborted recipe with "does not match any systems" result
* External watchdog / reservesys: mock {{/distribution/reservesys}} task with watchdog result; verify ignored vs non-reservesys
* Skip destructive tasks: enable {{skip_destructive}}, verify task removal in clone XML and last-task protection

*1c. Migrate to stdlib*
* Replace {{import lxml.etree}} with {{import xml.etree.ElementTree}}
* Replace type hints, parsing, serialization, SubElement (identical APIs)
* Refactor {{xpath}} -> {{findall}}, {{getparent}} -> task-first iteration, {{getnext+remove}} -> parent-context iteration
* Update {{setup.cfg}}: remove {{lxml}}, {{types-lxml}}, pylint allow-list
* Update 10 test parse helpers to use {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring}}

h3. Step 2: Add xmllint validation (BEFORE removing lint from kpet, ~2h)

*2a. kpet-db CI:* After each {{kpet run generate -o /tmp/job.xml}}, add:
{code}
xmllint --relaxng beaker-job-relaxed.rng /tmp/job.xml --noout
xmllint --schematron cki.sch /tmp/job.xml --noout
{code}

*2b. pipeline-definition setup stage:* Add same {{xmllint}} validation after the production {{kpet run generate}} call, so every pipeline run validates before Beaker submission.

h3. Step 3: kpet -- remove lint block and lxml dependency (AFTER validation is in place, ~2h)

* Remove lxml imports, {{InvalidSchema}} class, {{if lint:}} block (lines 918-938)
* Remove {{--no-lint}} CLI flag and {{lint}} parameter plumbing
* Remove {{schemas}} DB field from {{data.py}}
* Remove {{lxml}} from {{pyproject.toml}}, {{S320}} from {{ruff.toml}}
* Delete {{test_schemas}}, regenerate golden files, remove ~145 {{--no-lint}} test flags

h3. Step 4: pipeline-definition -- remove lxml pins (LAST, ~30min)

* Remove {{lxml<6}} from {{requirements-python.in}} and {{requirements-builder.in}}
* Regenerate lockfiles
* Remove {{--no-lint}} from the {{raw_*}} debug path in {{setup.yml}}
* Close or merge !2610

----

h2. Ordering

Key constraint: Step 2 (xmllint validation) must land *before* Step 3 (removing lint from kpet).

The beaker-jobwatch track (Steps 1a-1c) is independent and can proceed in parallel.

# 1a: Harden .text comparisons -> 1b: Add tests for untested paths -> 1c: Migrate to stdlib -> 4: Remove lxml pins
# 2: Add xmllint validation -> 3: Remove lint block from kpet -> 4: Remove lxml pins

See attached PDF for full implementation details with exact line numbers and code snippets.

lxml is a C-extension wrapper around libxml2/libxslt. As a compiled dependency it has been a recurring source of pain, especially on RHEL 6 where prebuilt wheels are unavailable and building from source against the old system libraries fails. The history tells the story:

* *2024*: lxml pinned to 4.9.x because lxml 5 installation is broken on RHEL 6 ([infrastructure#305|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/infrastructure/-/issues/305]). A Python-version split was needed ({{lxml==4.9.4; python_version < '3.11'}} / {{lxml==5.2.0; python_version >= '3.11'}}).
* *2025*: Constraints reworked after the RHEL 6 Python version was bumped to 3.11+ ([rhel-backports#3|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/rhel-backports/-/issues/3]).
* *2026-05*: CI needed a special container image ({{quay.io/cki/python}}) with lxml compilation dependencies just to run constraint verification ([pipeline-definition !2570|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2570]).
* *2026-06*: Renovate bumps lxml to v6, [pipeline-definition !2610|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2610] fails again.

This is a lot of ongoing maintenance for a dependency that only two projects actually use -- and neither needs its full power:

* *beaker-jobwatch* uses basic XML parsing, tree navigation, and serialization -- all available in Python's stdlib {{xml.etree.ElementTree}}.
* *kpet* uses lxml solely for optional XML linting (parse + schema validation + pretty-print). The schema validation (RelaxNG, Schematron) is the only lxml-exclusive feature, and it can be handled by {{xmllint}} in CI instead.

Removing lxml eliminates a C-extension dependency from two projects and from the pipeline-definition lockfiles entirely, ending the cycle of RHEL 6 build breakage and major-version upgrade friction.

----

h2. 1. beaker-jobwatch: migrate to stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree

*Repo:* {{beaker-jobwatch}} | *Effort:* ~4 hours | *Risk:* Low

All lxml usage is in {{beaker_jobwatch/__init__.py}} (15 call sites) and {{tests/test_beaker_jobwatch.py}} (10 parse sites).

h3. Production code changes (beaker_jobwatch/__init__.py)

*Import (line 16):* {{import lxml.etree}} -> {{import xml.etree.ElementTree}}

*Type hints (lines 193, 216, 465):* {{lxml.etree._Element}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.Element}}

*Parsing (lines 232-233, 846-847):* Replace {{lxml.etree.XMLParser(remove_blank_text=True)}} + {{lxml.etree.XML(data, parser)}} with {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(data)}}. Drop {{remove_blank_text}} -- this code reads attributes and meaningful text only; whitespace-only text nodes are harmless.

*Serialization (lines 250, 898):* {{lxml.etree.tostring(elem)}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.tostring(elem)}} -- identical API.

*SubElement (lines 889-890):* {{lxml.etree.SubElement(parent, tag)}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.SubElement(parent, tag)}} -- identical API.

*XPath (line 584):* {{recipe.xpath("//result")}} -> {{recipe.findall(".//result")}} -- equivalent for descendant search.

*Parent traversal (lines 699-704):* The {{getparent()}} calls walk from a {{<result>}} element two levels up to check if the grandparent {{<task>}} has {{name="/distribution/reservesys"}}. Refactor to iterate tasks first, then check nested results.

*Sibling check + removal (lines 873-884):* {{getnext()}} checks if a task has a next sibling; {{getparent().remove(task)}} removes it. Refactor using parent context and index check.

h3. Config changes (setup.cfg)

* Line 14: remove {{lxml}} from {{install_requires}}
* Line 26: remove {{types-lxml}} from dev extras
* Line 69: remove {{extension-pkg-allow-list = lxml}} from {{[pylint]}}

h3. Test changes (tests/test_beaker_jobwatch.py)

* Line 14: {{import lxml.etree}} -> {{import xml.etree.ElementTree}}
* 9 {{_create_mock_xml}} helpers: replace lxml parse with {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(xml_str)}}
* Line 1201-1202: same parse replacement in reschedule whiteboard assertion

h3. Behavioral notes

* {{remove_blank_text=True}} has no stdlib equivalent. Risk is low: only {{.text}} on {{<whiteboard>}} (JSON) is sensitive, and production Beaker XML is compact.
* {{xpath()}}, {{getparent()}}, {{getnext()}} paths have *no test coverage* -- the refactored code should be verified manually.

----

h2. 2. kpet: remove lint block and lxml dependency

*Repo:* {{kpet}} | *Effort:* ~2 hours | *Risk:* Low (validation moves to kpet-db CI)

All lxml usage is in {{kpet/run.py}} lines 918-938 (the {{if lint:}} block). Production pipeline-definition calls {{kpet run generate}} *without* {{--no-lint}}, so the linted (pretty-printed, schema-validated) output is what reaches Beaker today.

h3. Code changes

*kpet/run.py:*
* Remove imports (lines 22-23): {{from lxml import etree}} / {{from lxml import isoschematron}}
* Remove {{InvalidSchema}} exception class (lines 674-675)
* Remove the {{lint}} parameter from {{generate()}} (line 871), its assert (line 873), and docstring mention
* Remove the entire {{if lint:}} block (lines 918-938)
* {{generate()}} now simply returns {{template.render(params)}}

*kpet/cmd_run.py:*
* Remove {{--no-lint}} argument definition (lines 237-240)
* Remove {{lint=not args.no_lint}} from {{scenario.generate()}} call (lines 479-481)

*kpet/data.py:*
* Remove {{SCHEMA_PATH_SCHEMA}} (lines 700-702)
* Remove {{schemas}} field from {{Base.SCHEMA}} (lines 716-718)

h3. Config changes

* {{pyproject.toml}} line 26: remove {{"lxml"}} from dependencies
* {{ruff.toml}} line 230: remove {{"S320"}} from ignore list

h3. Test changes

* {{tests/test_integration_misc.py}}: delete entire {{test_schemas}} method (lines 1834-2226, 14 fixtures)
* {{tests/test_cmd_run.py}}: {{test_generate}} (line 48) calls {{generate(lint=True)}} and compares against golden files -- regenerate golden files from unlinted output, remove {{lint=True}}
* ~145 {{--no-lint}} flags across 10 integration test files: remove all (flag no longer exists)

h3. Output format impact

With lint removed, {{generate()}} returns raw Jinja2 output instead of lxml's pretty-printed XML with declaration. Beaker tolerates whitespace differences. The {{raw_*}} debug artifact in pipeline-definition becomes identical to the production artifact.

----

h2. 3. kpet-db: add xmllint validation to CI

*Repo:* {{kpet-db}} | *Effort:* ~2 hours | *Risk:* Low

Production kpet-db ships {{beaker-job-relaxed.rng}} (RelaxNG) and {{cki.sch}} (Schematron), referenced in {{index.yaml}}. The existing CI already runs {{kpet run generate}} for every tree/arch combination.

h3. Changes

* In {{.gitlab-ci.yml}}, after each {{kpet run generate -o /tmp/job.xml}}, add:

{code}
xmllint --relaxng beaker-job-relaxed.rng /tmp/job.xml --noout
xmllint --schematron cki.sch /tmp/job.xml --noout
{code}

* Verify {{xmllint}} (from {{libxml2}}) is in the CI image
* Decide on {{schemas:}} in {{index.yaml}}: remove it (kpet no longer reads it) or leave as documentation

----

h2. 4. pipeline-definition: remove lxml pins

*Repo:* {{pipeline-definition}} | *Effort:* ~30 min | *Risk:* None

* Remove {{lxml<6}} from {{requirements-python.in}} and {{requirements-builder.in}}
* Regenerate lockfiles

# kpet: remove lint block -> kpet-db: add xmllint CI step -> pipeline-definition: drop lxml pins

h2. Safety Analysis

Three risks were identified and each has a mitigation:

h3. Risk 1: Whitespace in .text comparisons (beaker-jobwatch)

{code}if task.text == "External Watchdog Expired":{code}

*Mitigation:* Normalize to {{(task.text or "").strip() == "External Watchdog Expired"}}. This is safe to land pre-migration and protects against Beaker output format changes regardless.

h3. Risk 2: Three untested lxml-specific code paths (beaker-jobwatch)

*Mitigation:* Add tests for these paths _before_ refactoring. Tests pass with lxml first, then pass again with stdlib -- proving equivalence.

h3. Risk 3: Losing schema validation safety net (kpet)

* Refactor {{xpath}} -> {{findall}}, {{getparent}} -> task-first iteration, {{getnext+remove}} -> parent-context iteration
* Update {{setup.cfg}}: remove {{lxml}}, {{types-lxml}}, pylint allow-list
* Update 10 test parse helpers to use {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring}}

h3. Step 2: Add xmllint validation (BEFORE removing lint from kpet, ~2h)

*2a. kpet-db CI:* After each {{kpet run generate -o /tmp/job.xml}}, add:
{code}
xmllint --relaxng beaker-job-relaxed.rng /tmp/job.xml --noout
xmllint --schematron cki.sch /tmp/job.xml --noout
{code}

*2b. pipeline-definition setup stage:* Add same {{xmllint}} validation after the production {{kpet run generate}} call, so every pipeline run validates before Beaker submission.

* Remove lxml imports, {{InvalidSchema}} class, {{if lint:}} block (lines 918-938)
* Remove {{--no-lint}} CLI flag and {{lint}} parameter plumbing
* Remove {{schemas}} DB field from {{data.py}}
* Remove {{lxml}} from {{pyproject.toml}}, {{S320}} from {{ruff.toml}}
* Delete {{test_schemas}}, regenerate golden files, remove ~145 {{--no-lint}} test flags

* Regenerate lockfiles
* Remove {{--no-lint}} from the {{raw_*}} debug path in {{setup.yml}}
* Close or merge !2610

lxml is a C-extension wrapper around libxml2/libxslt. As a compiled dependency it has been a recurring source of pain, especially on RHEL 6 where prebuilt wheels are unavailable and building from source against the old system libraries fails. The history tells the story:

* *2024*: lxml pinned to 4.9.x because lxml 5 installation is broken on RHEL 6 ([infrastructure#305|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/infrastructure/-/issues/305]). A Python-version split was needed ({{lxml==4.9.4; python_version < '3.11'}} / {{lxml==5.2.0; python_version >= '3.11'}}).
* *2025*: Constraints reworked after the RHEL 6 Python version was bumped to 3.11+ ([rhel-backports#3|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/rhel-backports/-/issues/3]).
* *2026-05*: CI needed a special container image ({{quay.io/cki/python}}) with lxml compilation dependencies just to run constraint verification ([pipeline-definition !2570|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2570]).
* *2026-06*: Renovate bumps lxml to v6, [pipeline-definition !2610|https://gitlab.com/cki-project/pipeline-definition/-/merge_requests/2610] fails again.

This is a lot of ongoing maintenance for a dependency that only two projects actually use -- and neither needs its full power:

* *beaker-jobwatch* uses basic XML parsing, tree navigation, and serialization -- all available in Python's stdlib {{xml.etree.ElementTree}}.
* *kpet* uses lxml solely for optional XML linting (parse + schema validation + pretty-print). The schema validation (RelaxNG, Schematron) is the only lxml-exclusive feature, and it can be handled by {{xmllint}} in CI instead.

Removing lxml eliminates a C-extension dependency from two projects and from the pipeline-definition lockfiles entirely, ending the cycle of RHEL 6 build breakage and major-version upgrade friction.

----

h2. 1. beaker-jobwatch: migrate to stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree

*Repo:* {{beaker-jobwatch}} | *Effort:* ~4 hours | *Risk:* Low

All lxml usage is in {{beaker_jobwatch/__init__.py}} (15 call sites) and {{tests/test_beaker_jobwatch.py}} (10 parse sites).

h3. Production code changes (beaker_jobwatch/__init__.py)

*Import (line 16):* {{import lxml.etree}} -> {{import xml.etree.ElementTree}}

*Type hints (lines 193, 216, 465):* {{lxml.etree._Element}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.Element}}

*Parsing (lines 232-233, 846-847):* Replace {{lxml.etree.XMLParser(remove_blank_text=True)}} + {{lxml.etree.XML(data, parser)}} with {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(data)}}. Drop {{remove_blank_text}} -- this code reads attributes and meaningful text only; whitespace-only text nodes are harmless.

*Serialization (lines 250, 898):* {{lxml.etree.tostring(elem)}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.tostring(elem)}} -- identical API.

*SubElement (lines 889-890):* {{lxml.etree.SubElement(parent, tag)}} -> {{xml.etree.ElementTree.SubElement(parent, tag)}} -- identical API.

*XPath (line 584):* {{recipe.xpath("//result")}} -> {{recipe.findall(".//result")}} -- equivalent for descendant search.

*Parent traversal (lines 699-704):* The {{getparent()}} calls walk from a {{<result>}} element two levels up to check if the grandparent {{<task>}} has {{name="/distribution/reservesys"}}. Refactor to iterate tasks first, then check nested results.

*Sibling check + removal (lines 873-884):* {{getnext()}} checks if a task has a next sibling; {{getparent().remove(task)}} removes it. Refactor using parent context and index check.

h3. Config changes (setup.cfg)

* Line 14: remove {{lxml}} from {{install_requires}}
* Line 26: remove {{types-lxml}} from dev extras
* Line 69: remove {{extension-pkg-allow-list = lxml}} from {{[pylint]}}

h3. Test changes (tests/test_beaker_jobwatch.py)

* Line 14: {{import lxml.etree}} -> {{import xml.etree.ElementTree}}
* 9 {{_create_mock_xml}} helpers: replace lxml parse with {{xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring(xml_str)}}
* Line 1201-1202: same parse replacement in reschedule whiteboard assertion

h3. Behavioral notes

* {{remove_blank_text=True}} has no stdlib equivalent. Risk is low: only {{.text}} on {{<whiteboard>}} (JSON) is sensitive, and production Beaker XML is compact.
* {{xpath()}}, {{getparent()}}, {{getnext()}} paths have *no test coverage* -- the refactored code should be verified manually.

----

h2. 2. kpet: remove lint block and lxml dependency

*Repo:* {{kpet}} | *Effort:* ~2 hours | *Risk:* Low (validation moves to kpet-db CI)

All lxml usage is in {{kpet/run.py}} lines 918-938 (the {{if lint:}} block). Production pipeline-definition calls {{kpet run generate}} *without* {{--no-lint}}, so the linted (pretty-printed, schema-validated) output is what reaches Beaker today.

h3. Code changes

*kpet/run.py:*
* Remove imports (lines 22-23): {{from lxml import etree}} / {{from lxml import isoschematron}}
* Remove {{InvalidSchema}} exception class (lines 674-675)
* Remove the {{lint}} parameter from {{generate()}} (line 871), its assert (line 873), and docstring mention
* Remove the entire {{if lint:}} block (lines 918-938)
* {{generate()}} now simply returns {{template.render(params)}}

*kpet/cmd_run.py:*
* Remove {{--no-lint}} argument definition (lines 237-240)
* Remove {{lint=not args.no_lint}} from {{scenario.generate()}} call (lines 479-481)

*kpet/data.py:*
* Remove {{SCHEMA_PATH_SCHEMA}} (lines 700-702)
* Remove {{schemas}} field from {{Base.SCHEMA}} (lines 716-718)

h3. Config changes

* {{pyproject.toml}} line 26: remove {{"lxml"}} from dependencies
* {{ruff.toml}} line 230: remove {{"S320"}} from ignore list

h3. Test changes

* {{tests/test_integration_misc.py}}: delete entire {{test_schemas}} method (lines 1834-2226, 14 fixtures)
* {{tests/test_cmd_run.py}}: {{test_generate}} (line 48) calls {{generate(lint=True)}} and compares against golden files -- regenerate golden files from unlinted output, remove {{lint=True}}
* ~145 {{--no-lint}} flags across 10 integration test files: remove all (flag no longer exists)

h3. Output format impact

With lint removed, {{generate()}} returns raw Jinja2 output instead of lxml's pretty-printed XML with declaration. Beaker tolerates whitespace differences. The {{raw_*}} debug artifact in pipeline-definition becomes identical to the production artifact.

----

h2. 3. kpet-db: add xmllint validation to CI

*Repo:* {{kpet-db}} | *Effort:* ~2 hours | *Risk:* Low

Production kpet-db ships {{beaker-job-relaxed.rng}} (RelaxNG) and {{cki.sch}} (Schematron), referenced in {{index.yaml}}. The existing CI already runs {{kpet run generate}} for every tree/arch combination.

h3. Changes

* In {{.gitlab-ci.yml}}, after each {{kpet run generate -o /tmp/job.xml}}, add:

{code}
xmllint --relaxng beaker-job-relaxed.rng /tmp/job.xml --noout
xmllint --schematron cki.sch /tmp/job.xml --noout
{code}

* Verify {{xmllint}} (from {{libxml2}}) is in the CI image
* Decide on {{schemas:}} in {{index.yaml}}: remove it (kpet no longer reads it) or leave as documentation

----

h2. 4. pipeline-definition: remove lxml pins

*Repo:* {{pipeline-definition}} | *Effort:* ~30 min | *Risk:* None

* Remove {{lxml<6}} from {{requirements-python.in}} and {{requirements-builder.in}}
* Regenerate lockfiles
* Remove {{--no-lint}} from the {{raw_*}} debug path in {{pipeline/stages/setup.yml}}
* Close or merge !2610 (the Renovate MR becomes moot)

----

h2. Ordering

beaker-jobwatch and kpet/kpet-db can be done in parallel. pipeline-definition cleanup comes last once both consumers no longer need lxml.

# beaker-jobwatch: stdlib migration -> pipeline-definition: drop lxml pins
# kpet: remove lint block -> kpet-db: add xmllint CI step -> pipeline-definition: drop lxml pins

items.fromString:
h2. Problem

Shadow checkouts from different origins often share the same kernel NVR except for the RPM distro tag on {{source_package_release}} (e.g. {{162.el9}} vs {{162.fc40}}). Exact {{filter_by_nvr()}} matching prevents grouping them, so:

* {{GET /api/1/kcidb/nvrs/{nvr}/status}} misses related checkouts when callers pass a release without distro suffix (e.g. {{kernel-6.16.0-rc7}})
* DW Combined View ({{?combined=1}}) does not aggregate stats across cross-origin shadow checkouts with different distro tags

h2. Solution (temporary workaround)

Add {{filter_by_nvr_without_distro_suffix()}} — a separate queryset filter that strips known RPM distro suffixes ({{.el*}}, {{.fc*}}, {{.eln*}}) from the release component before matching. Wire it into:

# {{NVRStatus}} API ({{datawarehouse/api/kcidb/views.py}})
# {{get_combined_checkouts()}} for shadow checkout grouping ({{datawarehouse/models/kcidb_querysets.py}})

Keep exact {{filter_by_nvr()}} unchanged for callers that need strict matching.

Document in code and {{documentation/api/kcidb_nvr.md}} that this is temporary until a first-class NVR entity exists in DW (CKI-7584).



This will work as workaround untill we fully switch to kqe tests.
